description: This figure is a single-panel table rendered as an image (no lettered sub-images, no axes, scale bars or legend), reporting estimated and experimental critical twinning stresses σt for one steel at two testing temperatures. Its six columns are headed "Temperature", "σt (M = 2.2)/MPa", "σt (M = 3.06)/MPa", "σt (M = 2.7)/MPa", "σt = (1/m)(γ/b + K/D^0.5)" — a Taylor-factor style estimate containing stacking-fault energy γ, Burgers vector b and a grain-size term K/D^0.5 — and "Experimental σt/MPa". Two data rows are present: for RT the values are 939, 1306, 1153, 1096 and 723 MPa; for LNT they are 742, 1032, 910, 934 and 778 MPa. In both rows the M = 3.06 estimate is the largest (1306 and 1032 MPa) and the M = 2.2 estimate the smallest (939 and 742 MPa), with the formula-based value falling between them. All four estimated stresses decrease on cooling from RT to LNT, whereas the experimental stress increases from 723 to 778 MPa. At RT the measured value lies well below every estimate; at LNT it exceeds only the M = 2.2 limit. The table therefore demonstrates that lowering test temperature lowers the model-predicted twinning stress while the measured critical twinning stress rises and approaches the predicted range.

observations.observation: The figure is a single table image with no panel letters, axes, scale bars or legend — it is not a plot or micrograph.
The table's six column headers are printed exactly as: Temperature; σt (M = 2.2)/MPa; σt (M = 3.06)/MPa; σt (M = 2.7)/MPa; σt = (1/m)(γ/b + K/D^0.5); Experimental σt/MPa.
The RT row reads 939, 1306, 1153, 1096 and 723 MPa across the five stress columns.
The LNT row reads 742, 1032, 910, 934 and 778 MPa across the five stress columns.
In both rows the M = 3.06 estimate is the highest value (1306 MPa at RT, 1032 MPa at LNT) and the M = 2.2 estimate is the lowest (939 MPa at RT, 742 MPa at LNT).
Every estimated critical twinning stress decreases from RT to LNT (939→742, 1306→1032, 1153→910, 1096→934 MPa), while the experimental value increases from 723 to 778 MPa.

At RT the experimental stress (723 MPa) is lower than all four estimates (939, 1096, 1153, 1306 MPa); at LNT the experimental stress (778 MPa) exceeds only the M = 2.2 estimate (742 MPa) and remains below 910, 934 and 1032 MPa.
The caption states that the table lists estimated and experimental critical twinning stresses in this steel at both temperatures.
The abstract states the steel studied is a low-carbon low-density Fe35Mn6Al0.1C steel tested at room temperature (RT) and liquid nitrogen temperature (LNT).
